title: Automated drift detection and safe rollback for on-prem upgrade flows
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Summary: Several recent on-prem upgrade incidents (customer escalations) stemmed from configuration drift between operator-managed Helm values and cluster-level customizations. Customers experienced partial operator rollouts, webhook failures, and services stuck in CrashLoopBackOff requiring manual intervention. This ticket implements: 1) an automated preflight drift check as part of the upgrade path, 2) an immutable-lock option for critical Helm values, and 3) a safe automated rollback pattern with fencing to avoid double-rollback and data loss.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Preflight job detects and reports value mismatches before applying Helm release for >90% of known drift patterns; 2) 'critical-lock' Helm chart feature prevents mutation of core values unless operator explicitly unlocked via API; 3) Automated rollback executes to previously proven release and marks a rollback annotation on CR and release; 4) Runbook steps for manual override are documented and tested in a staging on-prem cluster; 5) Telemetry emits drift-warning and rollback events to console and support dashboards.
implementation_notes:
Design decisions:
- Use a Kubernetes Job run by the operator to compute a canonical hash of 'managed' values and compare to cluster-annotated last-applied state.
- For checks that cannot be auto-corrected (eg. node label mismatches, custom initContainers), surface a blocking error with remediation hints instead of proceeding.
- Introduce 'helm.criticalLock' boolean in chart values that defaults to true for customer-managed deployments created after 2025-02-01.
- Rollback flow: operator will create a 'release-rollback' CR, set a RollbackInProgress annotation, then invoke Helm rollback with --no-hooks; after rollback completes the operator runs smoke checks (health probes) and clears the annotation.
- Add server-side rate-limiting on automated rollbacks to avoid rapid flip-flopping.
comments: 2025-01-30 - Maya Thompson: Initial triage summary attached to customer INC-8142. Root cause: customer had customized webhook certificate rotation cronjob which mutated the operator-managed webhookSecret name; operator upgrade replaced secret expectations causing cert mismatch and webhook rejection.

2025-02-03 - Rafael Ortega: Prototype preflight job implemented in branch feat/drift-preflight. It runs as a Kubernetes Job with binary 'ri-drftchk' and compares /etc/operator/managed-values.yaml vs annotation 'redwood.io/managed-hash'. Smoke tested in staging (k3s) against three scenarios: value drift, missing CR, node taint mismatch.

2025-02-06 - Priya Nair (SRE): Observability hooks created: telemetry events 'upgrade.drift.detected' and 'upgrade.rollback.initiated' forwarded to Datadog. Added dashboard 'Private Upgrades — Drift' for SOC and support.

2025-02-10 - QA: Manual test matrix executed in staging-onprem-1. Found a race where operator cleared managed-hash before Job persisted results; fixed by writing result as a ConfigMap with ownerRef and read-after-write guarantee.

2025-02-12 - Support (Evan Brooks): Customer acceptance criteria captured: must be able to opt-out of criticalLock for one-off emergency patches. Added 'unlock-token' flow to allow time-limited override via support console and audit log.

2025-02-14 - Rafael Ortega: Implementation branch merged to main; charts bump released. Started canary rollout to 4 Dedicated private clusters (non-production) to validate rollback fencing behavior. Next: schedule customer-facing release notes and update the runbook with explicit kubectl commands for manual rollback.

Manual rollback commands (to be added to runbook):
1) kubectl -n redwood get helmrelease <name> -o yaml  # get current release meta
2) kubectl -n redwood annotate helmrelease <name> redwood.io/rollback-requested="true"
3) helm rollback <release-name> <previous-revision> --namespace redwood --wait --timeout 10m
4) kubectl -n redwood annotate helmrelease <name> redwood.io/rollback-completed="<ts>"

Known limitations: database migrations are out of scope for automated rollback; runbook will require manual DB reconciliation in those cases.
